gao-gaoreports-gao-05-218g:
Framework for Assessing the Acquisition Function at Federal Agencies, GAO-05-218G of September 1, 2005, is a tool, not a probe. Agencies lean more and more on firms to do their work. Hundreds of billions of tax dollars buy goods and services each year. Weak buying wastes that cash. Buying at some agencies sits on GAO's high-risk list.

The framework rests on four linked stones. They are fit structure and strong lead, sound rules and steps, skilled staff, and good grip on facts. Top chiefs can grade their own shops with it. Watch groups can aim their probes with it. Each stone can stand alone for a tight check.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-568g: Guidance for auditors on the training duties in the federal audit rulebook is the whole of GAO-05-568G, issued on April 1, 2005. The short document, put out by the Comptroller General, helps auditors and audit organizations put the continuing professional education requirements of the 2003 revision of Government Auditing Standards into practice. Its indexed topics run to auditing standards, continuing education, and the Yellow Book. The hosted text is the guidance statement itself, in brief form.
